blocks.task_summary: Prove by mathematical induction that 5^(2n) - 2^(3n) is divisible by 17 for all n in Z+.
method_path: Verify base case n=1: 5^2 - 2^3 = 25 - 8 = 17, divisible by 17
Assume true for n=k: 5^(2k) - 2^(3k) = 17s for some integer s
Algebraically rewrite 5^(2(k+1)) - 2^(3(k+1)) as 17 times an integer using the inductive hypothesis
Conclude by induction: true for n=1 and n=k implies n=k+1, therefore true for all n in Z+
accepted_alternatives: 5^(2k) and 2^(3k) may be replaced by 25^k and 8^k throughout

evidence.basis: Base case n=1: 5^2-2^3=25-8=17 so true for n=1 [A1]. Assume true for n=k: 5^(2k)-2^(3k)=17s [M1]. Consider n=k+1 [M1]. Algebraic manipulation via EITHER/OR routes [A1,A1,A1]. Conclusion R1 with note: only award R1 if 4 of the previous 6 marks have been awarded.
